assertion: The American Farm Bureau Federation, in a July 16, 2026 publication, claims combined farm losses of $34.6 billion.
article_value: $34.6 billion, attributed to AFBF's July 16, 2026 report
warehouse_value: US net farm income (all commodities + govt transfers): $146.8B (2023), $128.3B (2024), $162.6B (2025 fcst), $158.4B (2026 fcst) — positive every year
independent_value: AFBF's actual July 16, 2026 report states $31B (2026) and $32B (2027) projected row-crop losses, not $34.6B. The $34.6B figure is AFBF's own Nov 24, 2025 estimate for the 2025/26 crop year, since revised by AFBF's own later report to a lower figure.

sources.title: AFBF News Release: Farmer Losses Projected to Deepen (Jul 16, 2026)
AFBF Market Intel: Persistent Losses Leave Farmers Needing Economic Support (Jul 16, 2026)

sql: SELECT "year", category, subcategory, amount FROM ag.ers_farm_income WHERE state='US' AND category='Net income' AND subcategory='Farm income' AND "year">=2018 ORDER BY "year"
score_claim_override_reason: score_claim's candidate_verdicts list ('accurate'/'misleading'/'false') does not map 1:1 onto publish_report's fixed enum, which has no 'misleading' option. score_claim's chosen value, 'misleading', sits between this report's 'partially true' and 'mostly false' on the same underlying finding (a real AFBF number, wrong report/date, and a metric narrower than its 'combined farm losses' framing) -- this is a schema/vocabulary mismatch between the two tools, not a substantive disagreement about the facts. 'Mostly false' is used here because the specific, falsifiable factual assertion under test -- that AFBF's July 16, 2026 publication itself states $34.6B -- is false (it states $31B/$32B); only the looser, unattributed 'AFBF has published a $34.6B estimate at some point' reading is true, which the report attributes in the fidelity Pinocchio explanation.
